articles.title: Eye on Everything
articles.summary: This article reports on significant internal club events, including the resignation of three board members (Rich Neuschaefer, Ed Erbeck, Bob Madden) following a debate over Mark Wagner's board status, and the subsequent election of Jack Zeiders and Paul Mancuso to fill two vacant seats. Additionally, two by-law amendments were passed, fixing officer terms to one year and requiring board members to also be club members. Other club news includes the need for a new homepage, the launch of a mentoring program by Ed Erbeck, and Jack Zeiders volunteering to lead the Observational Astronomy Class.

articles.title: Activities Calendar
articles.summary: The document outlines the San Jose Astronomical Association's activities calendar for December, including multiple star parties at various state parks and a general meeting with a speaker to be announced. It also provides a hotline number for 24-hour news and information, including details for January dates.

articles.title: Fun at Freemont Peak
articles.summary: The article recounts an astronomy observing session by Jay Reynolds Freeman at Fremont Peak State Park on November 9-10, 1996. Despite an initial cloudy start, the sky cleared, providing excellent transparency for viewing Messier objects with a 6-inch f/10 Intes Maksutov telescope. The author describes particularly rewarding views of the Pleiades (M45), including bright nebulosity, and the Orion Nebula (M42/43), noting its color variations.

articles.title: Fun, continued from page 1
articles.summary: The article recounts an amateur astronomer's night of observation, focusing on viewing various deep-sky objects including nebulae and faint dwarf galaxies. The author successfully observed the Sculptor and Fornax Dwarf galaxies, noting that a Wratten 12 (minus blue) filter unexpectedly enhanced their visibility due to their old, red star populations. The session also involved comparing different filters for nebulae, continuing a Messier survey with binoculars, and interacting with fellow astronomers and their diverse equipment.

articles.title: Eve, continued from page 1
articles.summary: The December 1996 SJAA Ephemeris features an editor's apology for delayed submissions and a detailed report on Jay Freeman's November general meeting talk about binoculars, covering their optical and mechanical properties and usage. The document also includes a letter of resignation from Richard W. Neuschaefer from the SJAA Board, citing his disapproval of certain board members' actions.

articles.title: Lunar Eclipse, West Valley College Rich Neuschaefer
articles.summary: West Valley College hosted its highly successful first annual Moon Festival, which featured a full lunar eclipse as its main attraction and drew between 500-1000 attendees, far exceeding expectations. Coordinated by Professor Tom Bullock and Jaime Ebright, the event included new age music, Chinese dancers, food, and over a dozen telescopes for public viewing, facilitated by SJAA members like Rich Neuschaefer. Attendees enjoyed views of Jupiter, Saturn, and the deep red/orange eclipse, making it a popular family-oriented community event despite late-evening fog.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: The SJAA Ephemeris, the official newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association, is published monthly. This publication schedule ensures 12 issues are released annually, covering the period from January through December.

articles.title: Henry Coe Park Status Jim Van Nuland
articles.summary: The primary observing site at Henry Coe Park, in use since the mid-70s, is being converted for a new ranger residence and will soon be permanently unavailable, though one last use is permitted on Nov. 16. The club is actively exploring new locations, with the overflow parking lot being the leading candidate despite potential light pollution and car headlight issues. An alternative corral site will also be investigated for future use.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS, Nov 6, 1996
articles.summary: This article, dated November 6, 1996, updates observers on Comet Hale-Bopp, noting its continued brightening and visibility challenges for Northern Hemisphere observers near year-end, while Comet Tabur unexpectedly faded. It also forecasts the visibility of several comets throughout 1997, including Hale-Bopp, Periodic Comet Wild 2, Wirtanen, Encke, Hartley 2, and Tempel-Tuttle, with some expected to reach binocular visibility.

articles.title: Ephemerides
articles.summary: This document provides ephemerides for Comet C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp) for a period between late November and early January, listing its Right Ascension, Declination, elongation from the Sun, and estimated sky magnitude at 00 UT for specific dates. It also indicates that similar data for Comet C/1996 Q1 (Tabur) would follow. This data is crucial for astronomers to locate and observe these celestial objects.

articles.title: Orbital Elements
articles.summary: This document presents a comparative table of orbital elements for two celestial objects, Comet Hale-Bopp and Comet Tabur. It details parameters such as perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, and orbital period for each object, along with their respective Minor Planet Center (MPC) references.

articles.title: Richard Stanton
articles.summary: This document, titled 'Richard Stanton' and part of the SJAA EPHEMERIS for December 1996, provides detailed astronomical data for celestial bodies over a monthly period. It includes lunar phases and rise/set times, as well as positions (RA/Dec), magnitudes, distances, and rise/transit/set times for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and the Sun. Additionally, it lists astronomical twilight times and sidereal time, highlighting 'Darkest Saturday Night' for observational planning.

articles.title: Astro Ads
articles.summary: This document is a collection of classified advertisements offering various used astronomical equipment for sale, including telescopes, mounts, eyepieces, and accessories. Sellers are listing items from brands such as Celestron, Astro-Physics, Takahashi, Vixen, and Orion, providing descriptions, prices, and contact information for interested buyers. It serves as a marketplace for amateur astronomers to find and purchase second-hand gear.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program Status
articles.summary: The article details the current status of a telescope loaner program, listing various telescopes, their borrowers, and due dates, along with information on availability and renewal policies for club members. It also includes an "Astro Ad" for a used Celestron telescope and instructions for submitting non-commercial classified ads.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document provides a directory of the officers and board of directors for an organization, listing their names and contact numbers. It also details the chairpersons for various committees and programs, including the Observatory Committee, School Star Party, Mentoring Program, Observational Astronomy, and Telescope Loaner Program. The content is identified as being from the December 1996 issue of the SJAA EPHEMERIS.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing fees for new or renewal memberships ($15 for general, $6 for junior) and an optional subscription to Sky & Telescope magazine for an additional $27. It provides instructions for submitting the form and payment via mail to the Treasurer or in person at an SJAA meeting. The form also includes fields for personal contact information such as name, address, phone, and email.
